h: A Darts Night in the New Town
p: St James Quarter puts you right at the eastern end of Edinburgh's New Town, with some of the city's best sights within a short walk. The Scott Monument, the huge Gothic spire in Princes Street Gardens, is just along the road, and you can climb its narrow spiral steps for views over the city if you've got the legs for it. On Queen Street, the Scottish National Portrait Gallery is a gorgeous red sandstone building filled with famous faces from Scotland's history, and it's free to get in.

Planning a group night? A few tips. Book for the right number of players and arrive a bit early so you can settle in with a drink. If you've got a big crowd, split into teams across a couple of oches. And decide before you start who's picking the games, because otherwise you'll spend half your time deciding.

New to darts? Stand side-on to the board, keep your elbow still and let your forearm do the work. Release the dart smoothly and follow through. Easy to say, harder to do, but the scoring tech means you don't have to worry about maths.

Edinburgh is a city that's made for evenings out. After your session, head to Broughton Street or the West End for food and drinks, or take a stroll up Calton Hill to see the city lights. Either way, a night of darts is a fun addition to any trip to the capital.
